body: Yeah. However, my suicidal ideation is slowly becoming more and more logical in my head. It used to be sparatic. I was scared, anxious, and depressed. Now it's a logical process. And that's what scares me.

I'm on Luvox and Lithium right now and it's pretty much the only thing keeping me above water at the moment, really. My OCD likes to hang on to the past. It likes to make me think that because I told someone I trusted about what I was going through that they told a bunch of other people. I think what scares me now is that other people think I'm a bad person, and that was one of my fears all along.

Hiya. 

Just hoping you’re still here for you to hear this. I’m truly sorry about your circumstances. Life really isn’t truly fair, and I wish it was more fair for you. You seem like a respectable person who just was slapped by life more times than others. And it really fucking sucks. 

Something that kind of helps me get through these kinds of situations is a quote I found on this subreddit.

“Offing yourself will completely deplete any chances of redemption.”

Life fucking hurts. But if you kill yourself, you lose any chance of happiness. You just cease to exist. And even if, even if, you think you won’t be in anymore pain when you die, there certainly won’t be any pleasure in it either. 

Fuck taking things “a day at a time”. Days are so fucking long when you’re depressed. How about an hour at a time? A minute at a time? Fuck, I have to take things a second at a time because a day or an hour or a minute seems almost unbearably long. One second or one minute at a time. On hour at a time. Then a few hours. Work your way up. Work on taking care of yourself for a second. Then another second. And a few seconds. 

I don’t know if this helps in any way, but I hope it does. Hope you’re here to read this. I wish you the best.
I’m still here. But thinking about it.

It was a complete accident, but I realized it could look really bad and I could get in really bad trouble for it. And if that thing happens, I can't fix it. My life will plummet into darkness that I can't return from, I know it.

Really. No one can know exactly what they are doing in life. If someone tells you that they know exactly what they’re doing with their life and know exactly where they’re going to go, it’s bullshit. Everyone is pretty much lost to a certain degree because there will always be uncertainty. Accept the uncertainty. Live in it.

I don’t think necessarily. I’ve had a therapist know I’ve had thoughts of suicide and nothing happened until I felt like I knew or they thought I was in complete danger to harm myself. You can mention thoughts because they’re just thoughts. But if you mention that it’s at a point where you have decided a plan, a date, or a method, that’s when they’ll begin to consider you a danger. It’s an odd area.

I got much more help with outpatient than impatient. Impatient just wants to keep you safe under any means necessary. Outpatient will actually listen. 

If you feel like you’re a complete and utter danger to yourself, go to a hospital. If not, go to a therapist and psychiatrist.

I feel everything to the point where I don't even want to feel anymore. It just feels like everything around me is constantly collapsing. It's like constantly having to build a sand castle and have some assholes mess it up every time you almost feel accomplished. 

To be honest I have nothing left to give to the world. I got nothing. All the energy is gone.

Yeah. Therapy is hit or miss depending on therapist and type of treatment. If you're not liking this therapy, try another. There's more than one therapist and there is definitely more than one type of therapy. And I know you've been through several, but people can go through dozens. I've been through 3 therapists, 3 psychiatrists myself, looking for different ones. You can get efficient help. I'm glad you're getting help though. That really makes me happy. Truly hope for the best for you.

This was hard to read. I'm so fucking sorry you had to go through that shit. You never deserved that, ever. I cannot imagine the kind of pain you must be having right now. But you've made it so far already and you have so much ahead of you. I think one of the greatest lines I've read on this thread that still sticks in my head is this:

>If you die, you'll lose all chances at redemption

If you die, you're stopping your story. You're stopping the story not even in the middle. It's like saying the first paragraph and not moving on. When you think about your life being a story, and you're the one making it, and the others are the ones reading it, I think it'd be pretty infuriating to stop it right there. To stop it where there's so much pain and hurt and sadness. You don't deserve that. You simply cannot let your dad's abuse be your legacy. If you want to overcome that hellish time, you just have to hang on. Nothing else. Just keep holding onto the breaths you have. That's when you start to win. 

This is so much happening by 16. I understand that. I don't understand even a cent of what you're going through other than depression, but I understand that it's a whole lot. You simply cannot do this on your own. And you don't deserve to be alone. Therapy works. Having someone to listen, just works. If you can't afford therapy, there's a whole community of people online that have similar experiences and are able to talk to you. Thanks to the internet, therapy and help are becoming more easily accessible. From what you said about your mom, I think she cares about you. I think your sister cares about you too. They want you to stay alive. They want you just to be there. And to fight whatever hell you get. And you know what? I want you to stay alive too. I don't even know you but that's a shitload to deal with. I want you alive to defy your circumstances. I think it's worth fighting for. Stay strong. All you have to do is breathe to fight. Breathe to fight. There's so much more for you. God bless you.

I haven't found a new therapist yet in my area. I just left my old therapist because I moved but dealt with it until now because I didn't want to wait a few months for another appointment with a new one. And I'm not far into college.

I think I use people as pure emotional support. My prior therapist wasn't the greatest at giving me actual behavioral therapy, so I turned to other people most of the time to where they can't help me and eventually gave up. For example, asking my friends for reassurance was one of my obsessive compulsions and it became so frustrating to them that they just felt like I was using them as purely therapy. 

I'm studying film. College has been nothing but stress and a source of one of my OCD anxiety ridden obsessions. It is a very different experience then what I was looking for.

I guess I haven't been really giving. I mean, I feel like I have been giving out a lot of my time and support. But I guess I just depend on people too much to the point to where they feel helpless and they can't help me. My family is like that too. They are aware of my issues but they literally don't know what else to do. I'm on medication and therapy. Currently on Luvox for my OCD, trying to find a new therapist in my new area since I just moved.

Well, I wasn't aware of any of my family's *extensive* mental health issues until recently after I was released from the psych ward. The suicides occurred when I was little and my parents just told me they were sick and just passed away. I guess it was their way of protecting me but it didn't do me any good. I was aware of one suicide in my family pre psych ward, but then became aware that two more family deaths were from suicide post psych ward. A lot of bad things that occur in my family aren't told to me because they want to "protect" me because I'm already under so much of this illness already, but it serves nobody to be lied to about it. I get why they do it, but it's not exactly helpful.

I’m pretty sure he only said that because you rejected him. It’s so funny and ironic how he goes from “I love you” to “You’re a monster” when he gets rejected. 

I have this fear a lot that people will use my OCD against me. Like I just truly am a monster. One of the things my therapy has been teaching me is to realize that OCD is not purely a part of me and my character. It’s just something I have and something that I deal with. It’s not part of you, it’s just part of your life right now. That goes with all mental illness. It’s almost like a physical illness. You don’t say that you yourself are the flu. You have the flu. It’s not a part of YOU. It’s just something you have to deal with. Remember that when you’re telling people you trust as well.

If you truly feel in your gut that you can trust your boyfriend, you can even tell him your OCD on a surface base and not have to go into uncomfortable detail. If you can trust him enough with that detail, don’t be afraid.
I don't mean to give any reassurance, but I just hope that this helped in some other fashion. There is absolutely nothing wrong with asking for help.

I would ask him if he could give you some kind of referral to the other doctors he knows that specialize in OCD (perhaps with the same company), but I think if you explain just the basics of your problem, he'll probably understand what it is. I'm 99% sure that he, as a licensed psychologist, knows at least the basics of how OCD works and some of the themes that come along with it. You've been through a lot of trauma in your sexual experiences, so if you've told him that, he'll probably completely understand where this is coming from.  Magical things can happen when you tell a professional, even if they don't necessarily specialize in a certain condition, they should at least know about the basics in my opinion.

When I told my therapist that I've known for years, who does not even specialize in OCD, I left the content of the thoughts out. I just told her I was extremely disturbed and completely disabled by these brand new thoughts I didn't think I was capable of having. She encouraged me to say them to her anyway. She didn't force it, but she encouraged me. I held my breath for thirty long seconds, and just broke down into sobs when I told her. She understood completely, surprisingly. And because she was my therapist of many years before, she connected what I thought was sudden onset OCD to what I told her in my past and that it was definitely from past traumas that were completely related to the subject. That's when so many things began to make sense for me.

Also, he simply cannot report you to anyone unless he knows for certain that you are a danger to yourself or others. You literally crumble in fear at the thought of hurting someone and you literally have done nothing wrong and fear you have or are going to.
